backendNote: setuptools 68.0.0 -- last release admitting Python 3.7. Unlike the 3.6 family's setuptools 59.6.0, this is post-setuptools-61 and reads PEP 621 [project] natively, so the metadata lives in pyproject.toml and setup.cfg carries only the mutmut and pytest sections.
packageManagerNote: uv 0.12.9 REFUSES Python 3.7: "Python 3.7.17 is not supported. Please use Python 3.8 or newer." uv 0.0.5, its first release, already declared >=3.8, and `uv python install 3.7` fails because python-build-standalone's floor is 3.8. Moving the family up one minor version did not help and will not until 3.8.

toolsActiveDetail.note: radon 6.0.1 declares no Requires-Python and imports cleanly on 3.7.

lizard 1.24.0 declares no Requires-Python and, on 3.7, imports and runs. On the 3.6 family it installed and then died on `from __future__ import annotations` in lizard_languages/zig.py -- that statement is legal from 3.7, so the same pin that was a silent trap one minor version down is a working tool here. Nothing about the distribution changed.
Not a PyPI package -- no distribution of that name exists. Implemented here as a stdlib `ast` cognitive-complexity scorer, written 3.6-compatible, so it runs everywhere in this corpus including here.
jscpd 5.1.1 is an npm package that runs on Node, not on the project interpreter, so the Python version is irrelevant to it. Verified in-session: found the planted clone pair in Python sources.
beniget 0.5.0 declares >=3.6 and means it. Verified in-session: DefUseChains and UseDefChains both build on 3.7. Needs gast 0.7.0.

ruff 0.16.5 declares Requires-Python >=3.7, so 3.7 is exactly its floor -- it is refused on the 3.6 family and installs here. It is the alternative tool for 19 of the 103 metrics, so this single minor-version step restores more cross-checks than any other change between the two families.

toolsInactiveSilent.why: pydriller 2.10 declares Requires-Python >=3.5, so pip installs it without complaint. It then fails at import: pydriller/utils/mailmap.py line 72 uses the walrus operator (3.8+), raising SyntaxError: invalid syntax. It failed the same way on the 3.6 family and will keep failing until 3.8 -- unlike lizard, which was a silent-import failure on 3.6 and runs cleanly here. A metadata-only support matrix marks this tool ACTIVE on both families. It is wrong on both.
